author: NorthEast News Desk
body: At least five people died and more than 80 were unaccounted for after a passenger ferry caught fire off Palawan in the western Philippines, the Philippine Coast Guard said Thursday.

Rescuers pulled 43 people from the water Wednesday night after flames broke out aboard the MV June Aster near Coron. Coast Guard footage showed fire engulfing parts of the vessel as emergency teams worked around it in the dark.

The ship’s manifest listed 117 passengers and 17 crew members, Coast Guard spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab told DZXL radio. Comparing that total with the confirmed survivors and deaths left more than 80 people missing, though officials cautioned that the number could change as search teams verify who was aboard and locate additional survivors.

The ferry had departed from Baseco in Manila and was bound for Coron. Authorities had not determined what started the fire as of the latest report. Search-and-rescue operations and the investigation remained active, making the casualty figures preliminary.
dek: The Philippine Coast Guard said 43 people were rescued after the MV June Aster caught fire, with the casualty count still subject to change.
headline: Five dead and more than 80 missing after Philippine ferry fire
